_readme: SAIRNroofing Phase 3a licensing/certification rule seed. OHIO ONLY, plus
the federal OSHA rules that apply in every state.
EVERY FIGURE READ FROM THE PRIMARY SOURCE -- the Ohio Revised Code and the
Code of Federal Regulations themselves, not a licensing vendor's summary.
Each rule carries citation, URL, verbatim quote and read_on date. Same
standard as sairndental_credentials_seed_ohio.json and
sairncare_compliance_seed.json.
── THE FINDING THAT SHAPES THIS WHOLE FEATURE ───────────────────────────
OHIO LICENSES NO ROOFING TRADE AT THE STATE LEVEL. ORC 4740.01 enumerates
exactly five specialty contractor types -- HVAC, refrigeration, electrical,
plumbing, hydronics. The word 'roofing' does not appear. Verified by reading
the statute, not by trusting the several secondary pages that say the same
thing.
This is the opposite shape from SAIRNdental, where Ohio DOES license and the
question was how long the licence runs. Here the correct answer for Ohio is
a negative one, and the danger is the mirror image: an app that quietly
generalises 'no state licence needed' to California or Florida would tell a
contractor they are compliant when they are not. Hence NO_RULE_FOR_STATE
fails loudly for every state except Ohio, and says so in those words.
── SECOND FINDING: NO-EXPIRY IS AN ANSWER, NOT A BLANK ──────────────────
OSHA does not place an expiration date on the OSHA 10/30 Outreach card. The
card is valid for life under federal law; refresh windows come from states
(NY, CT, MO, NV) and from general contractors. api/_lib/roofing-credentials.js
therefore treats has_expiry:false as the status 'current', distinct from a
record that is MISSING an expiry it should have ('unknown').
── WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED ─────────────────────────────────────
See unverified_notes. Manufacturer programmes (GAF Master Elite, Owens
Corning Platinum Preferred, CertainTeed SELECT) are COMPANY-level and are
not in this seed at all -- they are Phase 4 work per the scope doc, and
modelling them per-employee would misrepresent what they are.

data.label: Ohio — no state-level roofing contractor licence exists; only five trades are licensed
notes: The correct Ohio answer is a NEGATIVE one. This rule exists so the app can say 'Ohio does not license this trade' as a sourced statement, rather than showing an empty licensing panel that a user would read as 'not set up yet'.

This does NOT mean a roofer in Ohio is unregulated. Local registration, insurance and bonding requirements are set by individual municipalities and counties, and vary between them. Those are entered per-jurisdiction as 'local_license' records, because there is no statewide list to seed.

effective_from is the chapter's own era rather than a precise enactment date; the licensing-board chapter has been in force well before any date this app cares about, and no rule in this app turns on that boundary.

authority.quote: heating, ventilating, and air conditioning contractor; refrigeration contractor; electrical contractor; plumbing contractor; hydronics contractor — the enumerated specialty contractor types; the word "roofing" does not appear in this section

data.label: OSHA — fall protection required at 6 feet on low-slope and steep roofs
notes: This is a WORKSITE standard, not a per-employee credential, and the app must not present it as one. It is seeded so the training records that support it (fall-protection training, competent-person designation) have a citable reason to exist.
Roofing-specific: 1926.501(b)(10) covers low-slope roofs and (b)(11) steep roofs, each at the same 6-foot trigger. The permitted protections differ between them.
The app does NOT compute whether a given job complies. It records whether the crew assigned to it holds current fall-protection training.

authority.quote: Each employee engaged in roofing activities on low-slope roofs, with unprotected sides and edges 6 feet (1.8 m) or more above lower levels shall be protected from falling by guardrail systems, safety net systems, personal fall arrest systems, or a combination …

data.label: OSHA 10/30-hour Outreach card — no federal expiration; refresh windows are state or contract imposed
notes: The federal half is verified from OSHA's own Outreach program: the card carries no expiration date and OSHA does not require any worker to hold one — card requirements come from states, owners, general contractors and unions.

The per-state refresh windows above are recorded as LOCATED BUT NOT PRIMARY-VERIFIED. They came from a secondary compilation; the underlying statutes (e.g. NY Labor Law 220-h) were not read in this pass. They are stored as data a user can correct, and the app must not present them as confirmed law. See unverified_notes.
Ohio is deliberately absent from that map: no Ohio refresh requirement was found, and absence of evidence is recorded as absence of a claim, not as a confirmed 'none'.

authority.citation: OSHA Outreach Training Program — card validity
authority.quote: OSHA does not place an expiration date on the 10-hour or 30-hour Outreach Training Program cards; requirements to hold or renew a card originate with states, owners, general contractors and unions rather than with federal OSHA

verification_passes.scope: Ohio state roofing licensing (negative finding), federal OSHA fall-protection trigger height, federal OSHA Outreach card expiry.
verification_passes.method: ORC 4740.01 read directly at codes.ohio.gov; 29 CFR 1926.501 read at osha.gov. Search results were used only to locate the sources, never as the figure.
corrections: Several secondary pages assert Ohio 'has no roofing licence' without citing which statute establishes the licensed set. Reading ORC 4740.01 confirms it by enumeration — five trades, roofing absent — which is a stronger and differently-shaped claim than 'no licence exists'.

unverified_notes: Whether ORC Chapter 4740 expressly preserves or limits municipal authority to license contractors. ORC 4740.13 and 4740.14 were read and neither addresses local authority. The local-registration model in this app is therefore built on the observable fact that municipalities do register roofers, not on a statutory grant this pass confirmed.
The per-state OSHA card refresh windows (NY/CT/MO/NV, 5 years) come from a secondary compilation. The underlying statutes were not read. Stored as correctable data, flagged in the rule's own notes.

Whether any Ohio municipality's roofing registration carries a CE or exam requirement. Not researched — there is no statewide list, and enumerating Ohio's municipalities was out of scope for this pass.
Every state other than Ohio. Nothing is claimed for any of them, and the engine refuses by name rather than defaulting.
